cases.name: corpus-allow-python-heredoc-regex
cases.command:
cd /mnt/build/hook-corpus && python3 - <<'PYEOF'
import json, re, collections
from pathlib import Path
rows = [json.loads(l) for l in open("matches/pipestatus.jsonl")]
# how did PIPESTATUS appear: which spelling, and what did the command print for it
spell = collections.Counter()
empty_printed = 0
for r in rows:
    for m in re.findall(r"\$\{?PIPESTATUS[^ \"'\n]{0,6}", r["command"]):
        spell[m] += 1
    if re.search(r"(exit|EXIT|status|rc|=)\s*[=:]?\s*(\n|$|\s{2}|\])", r["result_head"] or ""):
        empty_printed += 1
print(spell.most_common(8))
print("sessions:", len({r["session"] for r in rows}), "first:", min(r["ts"] for r in rows), "last:", max(r["ts"] for r in rows))
by_day = collections.Counter(r["ts"][:10] for r in rows)
print(sorted(by_day.items()))
for r in rows[:6] + rows[-4:]:
    print("=" * 90)
    print(r["ts"], r["session"][:8])
    cmd = r["command"]
    k = cmd.find("PIPESTATUS")
    print("CMD…", cmd[max(0, k-200):k+60].replace("\n", " ⏎ "))
    res = r["result_head"] or ""
    print("RES…", res[-250:].replace("\n", " ⏎ "))
PYEOF
cases.why: A real Python analysis in a quoted heredoc whose regular expression and strings name PIPESTATUS.

cases.name: author-length-form
cases.why: Measured on this host: the length form answers 0, so the parameter is read and the answer is wrong. The match is on the parameter named, not on the text the expansion begins with.

cases.name: author-allow-longer-name-unbraced

cases.name: author-braced-longer-name
cases.why: A longer name is a different parameter, and it holds its value.

cases.name: author-allow-bash-c-escaped
cases.why: The backslash keeps the dollar sign literal in zsh, so bash receives its own working spelling.

cases.name: author-deny-bash-c-double-quoted
cases.why: zsh expands the double-quoted argument first, so bash receives an empty string where the array was meant.

cases.name: author-deny-bash-unquoted-heredoc

cargo test | tail -3
echo "exit=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"

cases.why: An unquoted heredoc fed to bash is expanded by zsh before bash reads it.

EOF
cases.why: A quoted heredoc fed to bash reaches bash unexpanded.
